title: Maratha Administration

cards.b: Shivaji (crowned 1674) built a compact, centralised, tax-based state. UPSC asks about the Ashta Pradhan, chauth and sardeshmukhi, forts, navy and the Peshwa period. It also appears with the Maratha Military Landscapes World Heritage listing.

Shivaji, born 1630 at Shivneri to Shahaji and Jijabai, took Torna (1646), killed Afzal Khan (1659), fought Shaista Khan (1663), signed the Treaty of Purandar (1665) and escaped from Agra (1666). He was crowned at Raigad on 6 June 1674 by Gaga Bhatt as Chhatrapati, and died in 1680.

A council of eight ministers, with no hereditary posts: Peshwa (prime minister), Amatya (finance), Mantri (the king’s records), Sachiv (correspondence), Sumant (foreign affairs), Senapati (commander-in-chief), Pandit Rao (religion, charity), Nyayadhish (justice). Ministers were advisers, not independent. Many held military commands.

Based on Malik Ambar’s ryotwari-type system with measurement by rod (kathi); cultivators paid directly to officials, not jagirdars. Shivaji abolished the role of hereditary deshmukhs. Chauth (one-fourth of revenue) and Sardeshmukhi (an additional 10 per cent) were levied on neighbouring non-Maratha areas, and in return protection was offered.

Cavalry were paga (regular, paid by the state) and silahdar (irregular, own horses). Infantry were the mavli. Forts: Raigad, Rajgad, Pratapgad, Sindhudurg, with three officers sharing power (havaldar, sabnis, karkhanis). The navy at Kolaba and Sindhudurg under Kanhoji Angre later. Guerrilla war (ganimi kava).

After Shahu (1707 to 1749), power passed to the Peshwas of Pune: Balaji Vishwanath (Treaty of 1719), Baji Rao I (1720 to 40), Balaji Baji Rao (Nanasaheb), who lost the Third Battle of Panipat (1761). A confederacy of Scindia (Gwalior), Holkar (Indore), Gaekwad (Baroda), Bhonsle (Nagpur) grew. The Anglo-Maratha Wars (1775–1818) ended it.

cards.h: Hindu swaraj or a revenue state?
cards.b: Nationalist historians such as G. S. Sardesai and Ranade praised Shivaji as a national hero. Marxists note a revenue-extracting state with peasant misery. Jadunath Sarkar was critical but also admiring. Debate also exists on whether he was a Hindu-nationalist or inclusive (he employed Muslims in his army and navy).

In July 2025 UNESCO inscribed the Maratha Military Landscapes of India (12 forts, including Raigad, Rajgad, Pratapgad, Sindhudurg and Gingee) as a World Heritage Site. Shivaji’s coronation anniversary is a Maharashtra festival. The Indian Navy’s emblem was redesigned in 2022 inspired by Shivaji’s seal.

• “Examine Shivaji’s administration.”
  • Prelims: Ashta Pradhan names, Chauth, Treaty of Purandar, Raigad.
  • Mains: How far was the Maratha state different from the Mughal?
